Expected losses and win probability for a single dice duel

Source: R/combat.R
rk_duel_odds.Rd

Summarises the exact outcome distribution of one Risk dice duel (see rk_duel_dist()) as expected losses and the probabilities of the three qualitative outcomes. No simulation is used.

Usage

rk_duel_odds(n_att, n_def, max_def = 2L)

Arguments

n_att

Number of attacker dice (1-3).

n_def

Number of defender dice (1-2; up to 3 in older variants).

max_def

Maximum defender dice permitted by the ruleset. Defaults to 2L; set to 3L for the older variant.

Value

A one-row tibble::tibble() with columns:

n_att

integer, attacker dice.

n_def

integer, defender dice.

e_att_loss

double, expected armies lost by the attacker.

e_def_loss

double, expected armies lost by the defender, equal to min(n_att, n_def) - e_att_loss.

sd_loss

double, standard deviation of the attacker's loss.

p_att_wins_all

double, probability that the attacker wins every compared pair, i.e. att_loss == 0.

p_def_wins_all

double, probability that the defender wins every compared pair, i.e. att_loss == min(n_att, n_def).

p_split

double, probability that both sides lose exactly one army. A split needs two compared pairs, so it is 0 whenever only one pair is compared – in that case p_att_wins_all + p_def_wins_all equals 1.

See also

rk_duel_dist() for the full outcome distribution.

Other combat: rk_battle(), rk_battle_odds(), rk_duel(), rk_duel_dist(), rk_odds_table()

Examples

rk_duel_odds(3, 2)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   n_att n_def e_att_loss e_def_loss sd_loss p_att_wins_all p_def_wins_all
#>   <int> <int>      <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>          <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1     3     2      0.921       1.08   0.811          0.372          0.293
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: p_split <dbl>

# One die each: a split is impossible
rk_duel_odds(1, 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   n_att n_def e_att_loss e_def_loss sd_loss p_att_wins_all p_def_wins_all
#>   <int> <int>      <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>          <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1     1     1      0.583      0.417   0.493          0.417          0.583
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: p_split <dbl>
